# Real garment photographs

These photographs are verification inputs only. They are never seeded into a wearer's wardrobe or shipped in the browser bundle. Each is the original downloaded file, without alterations. Browser and service verification resize and strip metadata from the account's stored copy.

All three files are published under [CC0 1.0 Universal](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/). Source pages identify the photographs as the authors' own work. The shirt and trousers show one garment; the footwear photograph includes black trainers and pink sandals, and the test wearer explicitly records the black trainers.

| File | Author | Original source and licence record |
| --- | --- | --- |
| top.jpg | Gmhofmann | [Faltbrett2, T-Shirt aufgelegt.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Faltbrett2,_T-Shirt_aufgelegt.jpg) |
| bottom.jpg | Ocdp | [Cargo pants 001.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Cargo_pants_001.jpg) |
| footwear.jpg | Alpha's beloved | [Shoes photo.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Shoes_photo.jpg) |

Downloaded on 2026-10-12. No model, fabricated image, mock garment, or image from the earlier GetYourFit prototypes is reused. The verification account's ownership and garment facts are controlled test inputs, not claims about the photographer's wardrobe.

`damaged.jpg` is the five-byte sequence `00 01 02 03 04`, created for the negative decode regression. It is deliberately not an image or a garment; the browser must reject it before any local classification request.
